idle_sample_anomaly_disclosed.assessment: 0 MHz is not a real operating clock and 0 MiB is not the real allocation. Both are IDLE-ROW ARTEFACTS of sampling a WSL2-passthrough dGPU from the Windows side: the Windows nvidia-smi does not account WSL guest allocations, and a deeply idle laptop dGPU reports a null clock rather than its floor. This is the same class of anomaly the A4 round recorded.
idle_sample_anomaly_disclosed.consequence: IDLE rows of the mid-flight clock sampler are NOT trusted and are NOT used as evidence of anything. Only LOAD rows (taken while contacts are in flight) are read, and they are sanity-checked against the physical envelope: an SM value must lie within the locked band and never exceed clocks.max.sm = 3090 MHz. Any load row outside that envelope is disclosed rather than believed.
idle_sample_anomaly_disclosed.observation: the Windows-side idle row immediately before takeoff reported clocks.sm = 0 MHz at 0 percent utilization, and memory.used = 0 MiB even though the resident llama-server (pid 2768) has the 30B Q4_K_M decoder loaded.
idle_sample_anomaly_disclosed.prior_occurrence: an A4-era clock-sampler anomaly reported impossible SM values on idle rows; carried forward as a known sampler limitation, not a GPU fault
